A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NIAT benchmark and synthetic-training work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. Reporting inconsistencies are identifiable document issues rather than extraction gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original NIAT evaluations, downstream fine-tuning experiments and training-task ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and fine-tuning results and adds evaluations of reasoning and multimodal models, including appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions synthesize coordinate-retrieval and six lookup/navigation tasks using GPT-4o and crafted CoT demonstrations, then fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B and Llama3.1-8B. Renaming the tasks and expanding construction details do not establish a changed training algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: v2 adds rendered table-image evaluation for both NIAT query types and cropped-table scenarios, extending v1's Markdown/HTML coverage. The four downstream benchmarks and three table structures remain. v1's separate cropped-plus-random-synthetic-table evaluation block is no longer reported.

E2.justification: v2 adds DeepSeek-R1 and QwQ comparisons, numerous multimodal baselines, TableLLM downstream results, and Qwen2.5-7B-Coder cropped-table results. TableGPT2 and GPT-4o also join the main NIAT comparison alongside the new StructLLM baseline. ALTER and TableRAG disappear; some long-context variants remain in cropped-table comparisons but are removed from Table 1.

E3.justification: The reported benchmark size changes from over 1,400 tables to 750, and main-text training size changes from approximately 15K to 12K examples. New image evaluation uses 120 tables per structure, with 3K-query subsets for costly API evaluations. However, retained appendices still give old table counts and 8,400 plus 6,497 training examples, so these reporting revisions do not establish reruns. The ablation control also changes its label from three to four downstream training datasets despite a conflicting caption.

E4.justification: v2 adds attention-pattern analysis in Figure 3, multimodal position/size analysis in Figure 6, and two fine-tuned-model case studies in Figures 7–8. The Llama training-task ablations largely remain, with a revised downstream-training control, while v1's Qwen ablation block is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's self-consistency voting validates generated questions rather than estimating uncertainty in experimental performance.

E6.justification: Many shared scores remain unchanged, but substantial result blocks are added or removed. New results include DeepSeek-R1's 51.17% accuracy on 32×32 cropped tables and Qwen2.5-VL-7B's 64.80% average cell-lookup accuracy. The mixed synthetic-table block disappears. The Llama downstream-training control's TABMWP score changes from 71.99 to 81.79 while its training label changes from three to four datasets; this is not a demonstrated same-setting gain.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies formal theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations. The coordinate and lookup task definitions retain their meaning; new attention explanations are qualitative.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the NIAT benchmark, diagnosis of weak cell-level comprehension, and benefits of synthetic training. v2 extends the diagnosis explicitly to multimodal LLMs and replaces the headline comparison against long-table agents with comparisons against specialist tabular models.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes RoPE distance decay and suggests table images as a possible remedy. v2 develops row/column attention-pattern explanations, hypothesizes visual-tokenization fragmentation, and interprets reasoning/coder performance through test-time scaling and structural similarity to code. Appendix A additionally identifies single-table and mixed-content limitations while retaining language and table-size caveats.

D1.justification: v2 adds evaluation prompt templates, templates for all six synthesis tasks, additional synthesis examples, explicit table sources including AIT-QA, and question-validation details. These substantially expand documentation. The Megatron configuration, two training epochs, vLLM deployment and eight A100-80GB GPUs were already disclosed in v1; neither PDF provides released project resources.

R1.justification: v2 updates citations for reasoning and multimodal models, AIT-QA, self-consistency, visual tokenization and table instruction tuning, while removing ALTER/TableRAG and several earlier methodological references. The central positioning against unstructured long-context benchmarks and high-level tabular benchmarks, including complementarity to LongBench-v2, remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark description and analysis are extensively rewritten. Separate synthesis, setup and results sections are consolidated into downstream experiments; task details and ablations move to Appendices C–D. Location-based/question-based terminology becomes cell-locating/cell-lookup throughout.

P2.justification: v2 changes to single-column layout, redesigns Figure 1, replaces the synthesis diagram with a benchmark-construction diagram, restructures Table 1 and separates the original combined results table. It adds attention, distribution, multimodal and prompt displays. v1's heatmap and CoT example remain as v2 Figures 4 and 11. v2 Table 3 also places cropped-table scores beneath unrelated downstream-task headers.

improvement.justification: v2 offers valuable multimodal and reasoning-model evidence, additional analyses and substantially better prompt documentation. However, its new 750-table and 12K-training-example claims conflict with retained appendix figures, the revised ablation has contradictory training labels, and Table 3 mixes differently defined results under misleading headers. These material gains and reporting harms leave the experimental provenance and net quality improvement insufficiently clear.
